themes.consensus_view: Banks broadly agree the trillion-dollar AI data-center spending boom is intact and spreading into power and industrial suppliers, while The Market Ear alone warns that Meta selling its spare computing capacity could be the first crack in the shortage story that justifies all that spending.

facts_agreed.claim: The AI infrastructure buildout is still accelerating, with hyperscalers committed to capital spending plans and demand outstripping supply.
evidence_quotes: the AI buildout is rapidly accelerating, which has clearly accrued to the immense benefit
The renewed capital-raising push confirms the industry is still in buildout mode
yesterday’s announcement shouldn’t make you adjust your 2027 Capex estimates materially
we think "chipflation" is more likely to reprice and ration AI infrastructure than derail the cycle
We do not need to know which AI model wins to know AI requires power.

facts_agreed.claim: AI capital spending is diffusing beyond mega-cap tech and semiconductors into industrials and power infrastructure, broadening the set of beneficiaries.
evidence_quotes: The broadening trade has real legs driven by AI capex diffusion into industrials/power infrastructure
value may start spreading beyond frontier AI labs and semiconductors
AI capex diffusion into industrials and power infrastructure

facts_agreed.claim: Memory demand continues to outstrip supply, driving increased capex investment across the memory supply chain.
evidence_quotes: Demand for Memory continues to outstrip supply, and recent datapoints suggest increased capex investments

themes.consensus_view: Ten banks reference ongoing US-Iran talks in Doha/Qatar and a possible interim deal as a live catalyst for markets, but none has staked a directional view on the outcome yet.

facts_agreed.claim: Banks across ten desks consistently flag active US-Iran diplomatic negotiations, hosted in Qatar/Doha and centered on a potential interim deal, as a near-term macro catalyst without taking a directional position.

themes.consensus_view: Most banks now frame the Fed under new Chair Kevin Warsh as tilting toward rate hikes and keeping rates high for longer, while Morgan Stanley stands alone in calling for no rate change at all through 2026.

facts_agreed.claim: Kevin Warsh is now Fed Chair and desks across the street are framing their entire policy analysis around how he will run the Fed.
evidence_quotes: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh policy task forces

facts_agreed.claim: The rate conversation has shifted hawkish, meaning expectations are moving toward rate hikes and rates staying higher for longer rather than cuts.
evidence_quotes: US Federal Reserve higher-for-longer rate expectations
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh hawkish policy meeting

facts_contested.claim: Whether the Fed actually hikes rates or simply stays on hold through 2026
facts_contested.for_evidence: our call that the Fed will remain on hold through 2026

themes.consensus_view: Six banks flag the ECB's annual central-bank gathering in Sintra as a near-term event where top central bankers will speak, but none of them has staked a directional market call on it.

facts_agreed.claim: Six banks reference the ECB's annual forum in Sintra as an upcoming catalyst this window, mentioning it as a venue where central bank leaders will speak without attaching a directional view.
evidence_quotes: Sintra forum panel with central bank governors
ECB Forum on Central Banking in Sintra

themes.consensus_view: Five banks flag the Strait of Hormuz reopening and the return of Persian Gulf oil shipping to normal as a live driver behind oil's slide, but none has staked a directional trade view on it yet.

facts_agreed.claim: Five banks reference the Strait of Hormuz reopening and the normalization of shipping and crude flows through it as a key backdrop for energy markets this window.
evidence_quotes: Hormuz reopening impact on energy markets

themes.consensus_view: Banks across the stack agree the US job market is holding up or even heating back up, and the shared read is that stronger hiring data pushes the Fed toward keeping rates higher for longer.

facts_agreed.claim: The US labor market is proving resilient, with multiple desks flagging a rebound or reacceleration rather than the cooling many expected.
evidence_quotes: rates market chose to focus on the labour resilience rather than the soft data spots

facts_agreed.claim: Stronger labor data is pushing markets to price a more hawkish rate path from the Fed.

themes.consensus_view: Banks agree the European Central Bank is heading toward its first interest-rate hike since 2023, with Goldman Sachs and Natixis both pointing to September as the likely start and nobody arguing against that timing.

facts_agreed.claim: Goldman Sachs and Natixis both expect the ECB's first rate hike to land in September, with the ECB seen as under less time pressure than the Fed.
evidence_quotes: broadly in-line data will be sufficient to convince the Governing Council to hike in September
Unlike the Fed, the ECB probably has the luxury of waiting until September.

facts_agreed.claim: Three more banks frame the current window around the ECB's first rate-hike cycle since 2023 without staking a directional call on timing.
